transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. I just... well, I manage an industrial production plant, and lately, things have been a little confusing for me. 

I'm usually really dedicated to my job, and for a while there, I was doing so well. I was launching these nonstop plant redesign projects, and I was calling our suppliers after hours to get things moving. I even rewrote the entire shift plan completely by myself. I thought I was just being really proactive and helping the team, you know? Is it okay to be that involved? 

But, um... the reason I actually made the appointment is that recently, I just... I suddenly haven't been able to keep up with the very plans I set in motion. It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I really want to be doing a good job and I don't want my bosses to think I'm slacking. I just feel terrible that I'm dropping the ball after starting all those projects. I was hoping you might be able to tell me if that's something you can help with?
During that time when you were taking on all those projects, did you need less sleep than usual?

Well, um... I guess you could say that. I really didn't want to waste any time, so I was maybe only sleeping... oh, two or three hours a night. But I promise it didn't make me bad at my job! I was actually showing up at the plant feeling really sharp and charged. 

It just felt like, at the time, sleep was sort of optional? Or just kind of inefficient when there was so much good work to be done. That's a normal way to feel when you're highly motivated, right? I really just wanted to do my best for the company.
During that time, did you feel unusually upbeat or euphoric?

Um, upbeat? Yes, I suppose so... at first, anyway. I felt, I don't know, almost electrically upbeat? Like I had all this positive energy and I was just so excited to share it with everyone and get things done. That's a good thing, right? Being passionate about your work? 

But then... well, I don't want to sound like a difficult person to work with, because I really do value my team. It's just that after a while, I started feeling... weirdly irritable. Like, if someone questioned one of my ideas or asked for clarification, it just felt like they were slowing down something that was so obvious and important. I feel awful even saying that out loud, because I know they were just trying to do their jobs. I was just so focused on the goal, you know? I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible.
Did that energized period cause serious problems at work or in other parts of your life?

Um... well, "serious problems" sounds a bit... I mean, I really always try to be a good manager. But, um... I guess things did get a little messy? I hope you don't think I'm incapable or anything, but... 

It actually got to a point where I had to ask to be pulled out of a shift-planning meeting. It's so embarrassing to admit this to you, because I really pride myself on my work, but occupational health ended up getting involved. I just... I suddenly wasn't able to carry out the basic production decisions that my entire role depends on. 

I felt terrible about it, like I was letting the whole plant down. I just want to get back to being a reliable employee, you know? That's something we can work on, right? I really want to fix this.
After that energized period ended, did you go through a time when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Um... well, after that whole occupational health thing... yeah. Things got really hard. I hope you don't judge me for this, because I really am usually a very positive, capable person, but... lately, I've just been feeling so down. 

I've been staying in this temporary apartment, and... um... I wake up every morning with this awful, heavy, hollow feeling in my chest. It's like the whole day is already ruined before I even get in my car to drive to the plant. I really try to shake it off, I promise I do, because I want to do a good job. But it's just there, almost every single day. Is it normal to crash that hard after being so motivated? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so we can get me back on track.
During this low period, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Um... I guess maybe a little? But not completely, I promise. I mean, I still try to do things. I don't want you to think I just sit around doing nothing all day, because I really do try to keep busy. 

It's just... well, usually I love going for a run after my shift, or trying out new recipes in the kitchen. But lately, in this temporary place, I just... I haven't really felt the spark for it. I'll get home and think about cooking, but then I just end up eating something quick and sitting on the couch. It's not that I don't *want* to like those things anymore, I just... I don't seem to get the same good feeling from them right now. 

I'm still trying, though! I even bought some new running shoes last week, hoping that would help. That's a good sign, right? That I'm still trying to do the things I'm supposed to do?
During this low period, have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Oh! No, um... no, definitely not. I mean, I know I just said things have been really heavy lately, but I promise I haven't given up or anything like that. 

I really value my life, and my career, and I want to get back to being myself. I would never... I don't have thoughts like that. I just want to feel better so I can get back to doing a good job at the plant. I'm really committed to working through this with you. That's a good sign, right? That I still really want to fix things and move forward?
During this low period, have you noticed your energy being low nearly every day?

Um... well, maybe a little bit? But I'm still getting up and going to work every day, I promise. I don't want it to sound like I'm just dragging myself around or not doing my job. 

I guess I just... I feel a bit more tired than usual when I get home. Like, after my shift, I just don't have the same bounce in my step. But I think anyone would be a little tired after working at a plant all day, right? It's just a demanding job. I'm still getting my work done and meeting my targets. I just... maybe I need a little more rest in the evenings right now. That makes sense, doesn't it? That I'd just need to recharge a bit more?
During this low period, have you noticed a clear change in your appetite?

Um... well, maybe a little? But I'm still eating, I promise! I haven't stopped eating or anything drastic like that. I don't want you to think I'm not taking care of myself. 

It's just that my eating has been a little... all over the place lately. Like, sometimes I'll be so busy at the plant that I'll look at the clock and it's 4 p.m. and I realize I've only had coffee all day. But I'm just really focused on my work, you know? And then other nights, I'll get home and just stand in the kitchen eating takeout straight from the container, even if I'm not actually that hungry. 

It's not ideal, I know, but I'm trying to be better about meal prepping. I actually bought some new Tupperware this weekend to help me get back on track. That's a good step, right? That I'm recognizing it and trying to fix my routine?
During this low period, have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual?

Um... well, I wouldn't say it's getting in the way of my job or anything! I'm still managing the floor just fine. But... I guess a couple of people at the plant might have mentioned something recently. I don't want it to sound like I'm slacking off, but they said sometimes I've been moving... well, painfully slowly. Like, someone pointed out that it looked like it took actual effort for me just to pick up a binder off my desk. I was probably just really deep in thought, you know? 

And then... well, sometimes it's the opposite. I really hope this doesn't make me sound unprofessional, but lately sitting still just feels kind of... unbearable. So I'll end up pacing around the production office, or I'll catch myself picking at my nails. It's just a nervous habit, really, from wanting to make sure everything on the line is running smoothly. That's pretty normal, right? Just a little stress from the job making me a bit restless or sluggish sometimes?
Did this low period last for at least two weeks?

Um... well, it hasn't been forever, I promise. I know some people get stuck in these ruts for years, but I'm really trying to pull myself out of it. 

I guess it's been... maybe around three months? Since things started feeling really heavy. But there's a good reason for it! I recently had to move for a new plant assignment, and you know how stressful relocating can be, right? Learning a whole new facility, meeting a new crew... it's just a lot to manage all at once. So it makes sense that I've been struggling a bit more lately, doesn't it? I'm sure once I get fully settled in, I'll bounce right back to my normal self. I just need a little more time to adjust, that's all.
